## Human review verdict — chalbert/web-everything#1500

**Verdict:** 🔁 changes requested

### Panel verdicts

| lens | weight | verdict |
| --- | --- | --- |
| correctness | mandatory | changes |

### Findings (1)

**correctness** (1)
- `scripts/operations/open-pr.mjs:214` — classifySubmit checks parsed.pr/parsed.url before parsed.reason, so a post-open refusal from pr-land (check-red, behind, conflict, check-timeout, the live-body empty-body recheck) is misreported as outcome 'opened' instead of 'refused'/'unrun'. — In `label-on-green` mode (one of the three OPEN_MODES this operation supports), pr-land.mjs opens the PR then waits on required checks. If a required check comes back red, pr-land emits `{ merged: false, reason: 'check-red', pr: <n>, detail: '...' }` (scripts/pr-land.mjs:980) — with a `pr` field, because the PR already exists by then. `classifySubmit`'s first content check is `if (parsed.pr || parsed.url) return { outcome: 'opened', ... }`, which fires before the `reason` field (mapped to 'refused' in HOME_REASONS) is ever consulted. I reconstructed classifySubmit verbatim and fed it the real shape pr-land.mjs emits for check-red (`{repo, merged:false, reason:'check-red', pr:1501, detail:'...'}`); the result was `{outcome:'opened', pr:1501, url:null, parked:null}` — a red required-check failure reported as success. The same precedence bug affects 'behind' (pr-land.mjs:981), 'conflict' (:975), 'check-timeout' (:986), and the post-open 'empty-body' recheck (:999) — all of which pr-land emits with a `pr` field attached, all of which HOME_REASONS classifies as 'refused' or 'unrun', none of which classifySubmit will actually report that way. This is exactly the failure class the PR's own description calls out ("One of the three [bypassed PRs] shipped with a red suite — precisely what #2833 exists to catch") — except here it recurs inside the very operation built to prevent it, in the CI-gating mode. No named test in open-pr.test.mjs catches this: every classifySubmit test for a 'refused'/'unrun' reason constructs its mock stdout as `JSON.stringify({ reason })` alone, never combined with a `pr` field, so none of them mirror the actual shape pr-land.mjs produces for these five reasons. _[CONFIRMED]_ _[impact if unfixed: broken]_
  - _Prevention (OWED — file it):_ Reorder classifySubmit to check `parsed.reason` (via HOME_REASONS) before falling back to the pr/url-implies-opened branch, so a refusal is never shadowed by an incidental `pr` field; as a durable gate, add a contract test that greps scripts/pr-land.mjs for every `emit({...reason: '...'...})` call site, extracts the field set each one actually passes, and asserts classifySubmit's outcome for that exact shape matches HOME_REASONS — so a new pr-land reason/field combination that the classifier mishandles fails CI instead of shipping.

---

**Decision:** `changes` — recorded by operator.
**Lens:** `correctness` — a SINGLE-LENS run. One `judge` step, one juror, one lens; the table above lists only the lens that judged. The other 3 panel lenses (security, simplicity, standards-conformance) did NOT run and are not reported as unjudged.
Net basis: `1f2ae138604e35e144956bdbdb7287beb62fb158..699d9271d3397622bc7f5814cf036d0fe83229f5` (rev `origin/lane/open-pr-operation` at review time) — 7 net changed file(s) vs current main (#2450), not `gh pr diff`'s three-dot list.

_Recorded through the declared `review-pr` operation (#3035)._
